evidence: The ALD experiments were carried out using a commercial flow-type hot-wall ALD reactor (ASM Microchemistry, F-120). Prior to film deposition, about 200 mg of the compound was inserted into the ALD reactor and was evaporated from an open crucible kept at 130 °C. Water was used as an oxidizing agent, which was evaporated from a container maintained at 25°C. The ALD chamber pressure was maintained at 1 -3 mbar during the depositions. Nitrogen (99.9999%, Air Liquide) was used as the carrier as well as purging gas. The following pulsing sequences (ALD growth cycle) were used: 0.5 -3 s pulse of Gd precursor, followed by 2 -5 s N2 purge, 0.5 -2 s H2O, and finally 5 -10 s of N2 purge.
